text: This course's closing lesson: one usable checklist pulling together all five chapters, built to review any lineage record you're handed, or any one you're about to build yourself.

Concepts — full path captured, business and technical views connected, column-level where it matters. Tracing — real source systems, specific transformation logic, all the way to final consumption. Dependencies — every downstream consumer checked, fragile upstream fields flagged, a real source of record when multiple systems overlap.

Documentation — findable by someone other than the builder, with a plan to keep it current. Applied practice — when something breaks, walk the lineage path backward instead of re-checking everything from scratch, and update the record itself after any fix, not just the code.

Every case study in this course shared one shape: an upstream change quietly broke an assumption nobody had written down. The habit that catches it earlier every time: check what's downstream before assuming an upstream change is fine.

That closes all 25 lessons of Data Lineage & Impact Analysis. The Data Governance path continues next with Master & Reference Data Management — deciding which system gets to be the one authoritative version of a customer, a product, or an account, that everything else defers to.
